absent: IPC permission evaluation and identifier allocation and lookup algorithms plus lock ordering between registry semaphore and object spin protection.
Message queue and semaphore and shared memory syscall behavior plus message segmentation and security hook interactions.
Full kexec load and relocation and crash capture flows including truncated callback parameters and architecture specific overrides.
Handover preservation and restore semantics when enabled plus scratch range management.
Kthread scheduling and freezing and work queuing and cancellation protocols plus timer handler effects and worker shutdown.
Notifier chain registration and invocation order and return code interpretation.
Reference counting and deferred reclamation guarantees for IPC objects and namespace teardown.
Sysctl table contents and limit enforcement for IPC and message queue tuning.
Compatibility translation details for compat descriptors and compat type widths.
Signature verification policy and measurement buffer lifecycle for file based kexec.

findings.text: The IPC permission header centers on a per object spin protection member named lock together with a deletion indicator named deleted. Identity is carried by numeric id and lookup key named key with ownership split across uid and gid plus creator copies cuid and cgid plus permission bits in mode and a reuse epoch in seq. An opaque pointer named security holds module state and linkage named khtnode supports key hashing while a callback head named rcu defers freeing and a counter named refcount tracks live references. Layout requests multiprocessor cache alignment and randomized field ordering.

An identifier registry for one IPC family tracks live population in in_use and a wrap sequence in seq with allocation bounds in max_idx and last_idx where the latter helps detect wrapping. Concurrency is mediated by rwsem while identifier allocation uses ipcs_idr and key lookup uses key_ht. A checkpoint restore build adds next_id as a deterministic allocation hint.

The IPC namespace aggregates three identifier registries in ids covering the classic families plus semaphore tuning in a four element control array named sem_ctls and a used count named used_sems. Message limits named msg_ctlmax and msg_ctlmnb and msg_ctlmni are paired with percpu accounting in percpu_msg_bytes and percpu_msg_hdrs. Shared memory limits named shm_ctlmax and shm_ctlall and shm_ctlmni accompany a running total named shm_tot and a forced remove flag named shm_rmid_forced that makes every segment behave as removed. A notifier block named ipcns_nb observes events and a retained mount named mq_mnt anchors the message queue filesystem with a live queue count named mq_queues_count. Message queue tuning exposes maxima in mq_queues_max and mq_msg_max and mq_msgsize_max plus defaults in mq_msg_default and mq_msgsize_default together with sysctl state in mq_set and mq_sysctls and ipc_set and ipc_sysctls. Ownership links through user_ns and ucounts while mnt_llist connects mounts and a common member named ns provides type erasure. Field order is randomized.

Each IPC object carries its own spin protection for short critical sections while each identifier registry carries a read write semaphore that allows concurrent lookups but exclusive modification of allocation state. Queue population in a namespace is documented as guarded by a dedicated message queue lock not shown here. Lifetime combines a reference count for prompt acquisition with deferred reclamation for readers plus a deletion flag that makes an object unreachable while references drain.

Conversion from the generic namespace handle to the enclosing IPC namespace is offered as a container retrieval through to_ipc_ns. One configuration provides null tolerant acquisition in get_ipc_ns that increments the namespace reference and yields the same pointer plus a not zero variant in get_ipc_ns_not_zero that only yields the pointer when a live reference could be taken.

An alternate configuration without namespace separation treats copy_ipcs as identity except that a request for a new IPC view is rejected as invalid. In that mode reference acquisition simply yields its argument and release does nothing while shared memory orphan cleanup does nothing and message queue namespace initialization reports success. Both message queue and IPC sysctl teardown are empty with setup reporting success.
The queue count default named DFLT_QUEUESMAX is 256. Message count bounds are minimum 1 under MIN_MSGMAX and defaults of 10 under DFLT_MSG and DFLT_MSGMAX with ceiling 65536 under HARD_MSGMAX.
Message size bounds are minimum 128 under MIN_MSGSIZEMAX and defaults of 8192 under DFLT_MSGSIZE and DFLT_MSGSIZEMAX with ceiling 16777216 under HARD_MSGSIZEMAX equivalent to sixteen mebibytes.

A segment descriptor named kexec_segment overlays a user pointer named buf and a kernel pointer named kbuf for the source buffer with separate lengths for buffer size in bufsz and destination address in mem and memory footprint in memsz. A compatibility variant named compat_kexec_segment mirrors this with fixed width compat types. A placement request named kexec_buf bundles the owning image with buffer address and size and target address and size plus alignment in buf_align and address bounds in buf_min and buf_max with an optional contiguous page in cma and a direction flag named top_down and a randomness request named random in crash builds. Purgatory metadata named purgatory_info keeps a read only executable header pointer named ehdr plus mutable section headers named sechdrs and a staging buffer named purgatory_buf that may be released after loading. Loader ELF info named kexec_elf_info keeps a caller owned byte buffer named buffer together with header pointer named ehdr and program header pointer named proghdrs.

A kexec image anchors a control chain through head and cursor pointers for entry building with a start address and dedicated control and swap pages plus a copy pointer for crash notes. Segment state counts active entries and stores parallel arrays of descriptors and contiguous backing pages plus three lists for control and destination and unusable pages and a next control cursor for crash reservations. Mode uses single bit flags for crash versus default and context preservation and file originated loading and hotplug update safety and contiguous avoidance with an architecture extension when configured. File mode adds kernel and ramdisk and command line buffers with lengths plus a loader table and opaque loader state and embedded purgatory info and a device tree carry flag. Hotplug builds add action and core header tracking while measurement builds add a virtual buffer with physical address and size and segment index plus validity flag. Handover state adds scratch and firmware table addresses while trailing members hold core header storage with size and load address plus a key blob address and size.

Image format handling is abstracted as a table named kexec_file_ops with callbacks for probing a kernel blob and loading it into an image and cleaning loader state and optionally verifying a signature when signing is configured. Probe consumes kernel bytes and length and reports suitability while load consumes the image and mutable kernel bytes and yields loader state with further parameters outside the visible prefix. Cleanup releases that state and verification consumes at least kernel bytes with its remainder also outside the visible prefix.

Control entry kinds use bit zero for destination under IND_DESTINATION_BIT and bit one for indirection under IND_INDIRECTION_BIT and bit two for completion under IND_DONE_BIT and bit three for source under IND_SOURCE_BIT with single bit masks named IND_DESTINATION and IND_INDIRECTION and IND_DONE and IND_SOURCE and a combined mask named IND_FLAGS covering all four. Image type zero under KEXEC_TYPE_DEFAULT means default and one under KEXEC_TYPE_CRASH means crash. File flags under KEXEC_FILE_FLAGS combine unload with on crash and no ramdisk and debug and no contiguous allocation and force device tree. Classic flags under KEXEC_FLAGS cover on crash with core header update and hotplug support in one variant and add context preservation in the other. Unknown placement address under KEXEC_BUF_MEM_UNKNOWN is zero.

Control memory allocation named KEXEC_CONTROL_MEMORY_GFP combines GFP_KERNEL with __GFP_NORETRY. Crash control limit named KEXEC_CRASH_CONTROL_MEMORY_LIMIT aliases KEXEC_CONTROL_MEMORY_LIMIT. Crash alignment named KEXEC_CRASH_MEM_ALIGN equals PAGE_SIZE. Entry type named kimage_entry_t is an unsigned machine word.

Architecture hooks default to shared implementations for image probing and post load cleanup and memory hole location while excluded range checking unconditionally reports success and post allocation and pre free hooks do nothing. Relocation handling for both addend and non addend forms reports an unsupported executable format error. Machine post load also reports success and instruction cache maintenance for a control page is empty.

Boot address conversions between page and frame number and physical and virtual forms are identity mappings through the standard page frame helpers in this configuration with virtual to boot physical going through physical address translation. Releasing a reserved crash range walks page sized steps and frees each backing page. Crash entry and crash predicate and crash loaded check and segment mapping and unmapping and signature enforcement are all neutral disabled stubs yielding zero or null or doing nothing and the in progress indicator is constantly false. Debug logging emits only when a global file debug flag is set.

One build randomizes a temporary placement start inside a caller supplied interval using sixteen bit entropy scaled across the span but only when the placement request marks itself random. The alternate build leaves the temporary untouched.

Handover state is fully disabled here with enabled and boot predicates false and overlap detection false. Folio and page and virtual mapping preservation requests fail with operation unsupported while their release counterparts do nothing and allocation for preservation fails likewise. Restore helpers yield null while subtree addition and retrieval fail as unsupported and removal does nothing. Memory initialization and population do nothing. Scratch handling either forces a contiguous migration type named MIGRATE_CMA on overlap or preserves the incoming type when overlap is impossible with disabled overlap making the first variant equivalent to pass through.

A worker named kthread_worker aggregates a flag word named flags with a raw spin protection member named lock and a ready list named work_list and a delayed list named delayed_work_list plus an owning task named task and a current pointer named current_work. A work item named kthread_work carries node linkage named node and a callback named func of type kthread_work_func_t with a back pointer named worker and a count named canceling for concurrent cancellation attempts. Delayed work named kthread_delayed_work pairs work named work with a timer named timer. A flag named KTW_FREEZABLE with value one marks a worker as freezable across suspend.

Thread identity in tsk_is_kthread is tested by checking a kernel thread flag named PF_KTHREAD on the task and yielding its private association named worker_private on match else null. Creation helpers bind a function and data with a formatted name to a node or processor and combined run helpers additionally wake the new task and propagate creation failure. Exit maps to task termination with a status. Static and dynamic initializers prepare workers and work items and delayed items including timer configuration while worker creation on a node or processor plus run variants follow the same create then wake pattern. Block layer association is empty.

Creation yields a dormant thread or worker that becomes schedulable only after an explicit wake with failure propagation preserving the error instead of waking. Work items exist in distinct static versus dynamic initialization forms that converge to a queueable shape with cleared linkage and assigned callback and bound timer for delayed variants.

Image mode is selected by single bit selectors distinguishing crash from default capture and file originated loading from classic loading with additional selectors for context preservation and contiguous avoidance and hotplug update safety. File mode extends the lifecycle with loader buffers and purgatory staging that are populated during load and may be released after while hotplug and measurement extensions add optional update and attestation states tracked by indices and validity flags.

A message envelope named msg_msg chains through m_list and selects with m_type and sizes text in m_ts and chains fragments through next of type named msg_msgseg and tags security with payload bytes following the header contiguously.
Notification callback type named notifier_fn_t yields a signed integer and takes at least a notifier block pointer with any further parameters outside the visible prefix.

The segment source pointer aliases user and kernel address spaces under different syscall paths through members named buf and kbuf so dereference must use the accessor matching the origin or risk wrong address space access. Compatibility descriptors use fixed width compat integer and pointer types whose sizes differ from native on some platforms requiring explicit conversion. Purgatory section and staging buffers are mutable temporaries that must not be used after load completes and the executable header pointer refers to read only storage that must not be written.

Lifetime state is split across a deletion marker and a reference count and a deferred callback head so readers relying on only one risk observing freed or resurrected objects. Identifier values combine index with sequence state so numeric equality alone does not prove liveness. Queue population and message accounting mix percpu and plain counters and work cancellation uses a shared counter both of which risk lost updates under concurrent access without external coordination.
Each header is protected against multiple inclusion by a unique preprocessor guard that makes repeated inclusion idempotent.
